thingsToDo.title: St. Johns River and Downtown Riverwalk
thingsToDo.description: Use the riverfront as the geographic spine for downtown, bridges, skyline views, museums, and boat traffic.

thingsToDo.title: Riverside and Avondale
thingsToDo.description: Explore historic streets, parks, restaurants, architecture, and local shopping in two of the city's most walkable neighborhood districts.

thingsToDo.title: Cummer Museum of Art & Gardens
thingsToDo.description: Pair the museum's collection with riverfront gardens for one of Jacksonville's strongest cultural stops.

thingsToDo.title: Timucuan Ecological and Historic Preserve
thingsToDo.description: Visit this National Park Service unit for marshes, waterways, historic sites, and a broader understanding of northeast Florida's coastal landscape.

thingsToDo.title: Kathryn Abbey Hanna Park
thingsToDo.description: Use this city park for Atlantic beach, trails, biking, lake recreation, and a more nature-focused day.

thingsToDo.title: Jacksonville Beach — separate city
thingsToDo.description: Head east for the oceanfront, but identify Jacksonville Beach as a separate incorporated municipality rather than a Jacksonville neighborhood.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

travelTips: Group each day by geography instead of crossing the region repeatedly.
Use early mornings for exposed outdoor activities and waterfront time.
Check park, marine, and weather conditions before nature-focused plans.
Treat nearby municipalities and protected areas as separate destinations with their own access rules.

faq.q: How many days should I plan for Jacksonville?
faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.q: Is Jacksonville good for outdoor travelers?
faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.
It depends on the destination, but a car or guided tour is often useful for protected lands and regional excursions.

faq.q: Should I book tours in advance?
faq.a: For high-demand wildlife, boating, park, and holiday-period experiences, advance booking is sensible.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Jacksonville is a consolidated city-county centered on the broad St. Johns River in northeast Florida.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: The river, Atlantic coast, tidal marshes, and barrier-island systems produce far more geographic variety than a typical city guide suggests.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Riverside, Avondale, San Marco, downtown, and historic sites reflect multiple eras of urban growth and regional culture.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: River recreation, beaches, marshes, biking, and the Timucuan Preserve give the city a strong outdoor identity.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: Jacksonville is geographically large; organize days by riverfront, historic neighborhoods, beaches, and northeast preserves.
